subject: AM
q: A bacterial culture increases from 4,000 to 12,000 in 2 hours. What is the hourly growth rate?
showNote: 100% is the simple (linear) rate; compounding hourly, tripling in 2 hours is √3 − 1 ≈ 73% an hour.
solution: It gains 8,000 in 2 hours, 4,000 an hour, which is 100% of the starting 4,000 each hour.

subject: AM
q: A laptop costs $200 and the seller offers a 10% discount on every 10 laptops purchased. How much is 40 laptops?

subject: AM
q: The perimeter of a rectangular roof is 48 meters, and its length is 3 times its width. What is its length in centimetres?
solution: 2(3w + w) = 8w = 48, so w = 6 m and the length is 18 m = 1,800 cm.

subject: AM
q: If a PDE has one real repeated characteristic root, then it is
solution: A repeated real root means B² − 4AC = 0, the parabolic case.

subject: AM
q: The surface of a square pond has a perimeter of 480 meters. What is the length of one side of the pond surface?
solution: A square has 4 equal sides: 480 ÷ 4 = 120 m.

subject: AM
q: What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of the quadratic function R(x) = −4x² + 16x?

subject: AM
q: What is the limit of sin x/x as x approaches zero?
solution: sin x ÷ x → 1 as x → 0 (a standard limit, from sin x ≈ x for small x).

subject: AM
q: The function f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) is discontinuous at x = ____
solution: The denominator is zero at x = 2, so f is undefined there.

subject: AM
q: The Laplace equation is a special case of the
solution: Poisson's equation is ∇²u = f; Laplace's equation is the case f = 0.

subject: AM
q: What is 1 micron in centimetre?
solution: 1 micron = 10⁻⁶ m = 10⁻⁴ cm.

subject: AM
q: The length of a pen is 36 cm and its radius is 8 cm. What is the ratio of its length to its diameter in its lowest terms?
solution: Diameter = 16 cm, so 36 : 16 = 9 : 4.

subject: AM
q: A man divides $360,000 in ratio 4:3:3 among his daughter and two sons. How much does the daughter receive?
solution: The ratio 4:3:3 has 4 + 3 + 3 = 10 parts. One part is 360,000 ÷ 10 = 36,000, so the daughter's 4 parts come to 4 × 36,000 = $144,000.
trick: The parts add up to 10, so one part is 36,000 (drop a zero). Four parts is 144,000. Neither $130,000 nor $140,000 is a whole number of 36,000s, so only $144,000 can be a share.

subject: AM
q: If 8 combination 3 = 56, what is 8 permutation 3?
solution: Permutations are combinations times the ways to order the chosen items: 8P3 = 8C3 × 3! = 56 × 6 = 336.
trick: Skip the 56 and multiply the top three numbers: 8 × 7 × 6 = 336.

subject: AM
q: In a 5-dimensional hypercube, how many 3-dimensional cubes form its boundary?
solution: A 3D cube inside a 5D cube is fixed by choosing which 3 of the 5 directions it spans, then setting the other 2 coordinates to 0 or 1. That gives 5C3 × 2² = 10 × 4 = 40 cubes.
trick: Pick the 3 free directions (5C3 = 10 ways), then fix each of the other 2 coordinates at 0 or 1 (2 × 2 = 4 ways). 10 × 4 = 40. The option 10 is the count of 4D pieces instead.

subject: AM
q: A committee of 3 must be formed from 6 engineers and 5 architects. How many ways can this be done?
solution: Only the total number of people matters: 6 + 5 = 11. The number of committees is 11C3 = (11 × 10 × 9) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 990 ÷ 6 = 165.
trick: Multiply 11 × 10 × 9 = 990, then divide by 6 to get 165.

subject: AM
q: Compute the number of 4-member committees with at least 2 girls from 5 girls and 3 boys.
solution: Total 4 member committees from 8 people: 8C4 = 70. Fewer than 2 girls means exactly 1 girl and 3 boys (0 girls would need 4 boys, but there are only 3): 5C1 × 3C3 = 5. So at least 2 girls: 70 − 5 = 65.
trick: Use the complement. 8C4 = 70, and the only bad committee has 1 girl and all 3 boys, which can be picked in 5 ways. 70 − 5 = 65.

subject: AM
q: A corridor shown as 8cm on a floor plan uses a 1:100 scale. What is the real-world length?
solution: Real length = plan length × 100 = 8 cm × 100 = 800 cm = 8 m.
trick: At 1:100, 1 cm stands for 1 m. So 8 cm is 8 m.

subject: AM
q: A beam has a mass of 40kg and a volume of 0.05m³. Find its density.
solution: Density = mass ÷ volume = 40 ÷ 0.05 = 800 kg/m³.
trick: Dividing by 0.05 is the same as multiplying by 20, so 40 × 20 = 800.

subject: AM
q: A microscope has an objective magnification of 40x and an eyepiece of 10x. What is the total magnification?
solution: Total magnification = objective × eyepiece = 40 × 10 = 400x.
trick: Multiplying by 10 just adds a zero, so 40 becomes 400.

subject: AM
q: A substance has a half-life of 5 days. What fraction remains after 15 days?
solution: 15 days ÷ 5 days = 3 half-lives. The fraction left is (1/2)³ = 1/8.
trick: Halve three times: 1, then 1/2, then 1/4, then 1/8.

subject: AM
q: Leaning against a building, a 13ft ladder reaches 12ft up the wall. How far is the ladder's base from the building?
solution: The ladder is the hypotenuse, so base² = 13² − 12² = 169 − 144 = 25. The base is √25 = 5 ft from the building.
trick: 5, 12, 13 is a well known right triangle, so the missing side is 5 ft.

subject: AM
q: Find the inflection point of f(x) = x³ − 6x².
solution: An inflection point is where the second derivative changes sign, so set it equal to 0. The first derivative is 3x² − 12x and the second is 6x − 12, which is 0 when x = 2. Then f(2) = 2³ − 6 × 2² = 8 − 24 = −16. The inflection point is (2, −16).
trick: For a cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d, the inflection is at x = −b ÷ (3a) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Only one option has x = 2, so you can stop there.

subject: AM
q: A radioactive sample reduces to 1/8 its mass in 48 hours. What is the half-life duration?
solution: After n half-lives the mass left is (1/2)ⁿ of the original. 1/8 = (1/2)³, so 3 half-lives passed in 48 hours. One half-life is 48 ÷ 3 = 16 hours.
trick: 1/8 means halving three times (2 × 2 × 2 = 8). Split 48 hours into 3 equal parts: 16.

subject: AM
q: A machine scales designs by a ratio of 1:12. If a part is 0.5m on the model, what is it in reality?
solution: A ratio of 1:12 means the real size is 12 times the model size. The real part is 0.5 × 12 = 6 m. So the answer is 6 m.
trick: Half of 12 is 6.

subject: AM
q: A ship sails 15km east, then 20km north. What is the displacement of the ship?
solution: East and north are at right angles, so the displacement is the hypotenuse. d = √(15² + 20²) = √(225 + 400) = √625 = 25 km. The displacement is 25 km.
trick: 15 and 20 are 5 × 3 and 5 × 4, so this is the 3, 4, 5 triangle times 5. The hypotenuse is 5 × 5 = 25.

subject: AM
q: A 1:50 scale bridge model withstands 200N. If strength scales with area, what force can the real bridge resist?
solution: Strength scales with area, and area scales with the square of the length ratio. The area factor is 50² = 2,500. So the real bridge can resist 200 × 2,500 = 500,000 N.
trick: Length 50 times bigger means area 50 × 50 = 2,500 times bigger. For 200 × 2,500, do 2 × 25 = 50 and add four zeros: 500,000. The other options are only 25 and 250 times bigger.

subject: AM
q: In a square field with 40m sides, find the angle formed between the diagonal and one of the sides.
solution: In a square, the diagonal splits the 90° corner into two equal angles. As a check, tan θ = 40 ÷ 40 = 1, so θ = 45°. The angle is 45°.
trick: The diagonal cuts the right angle in half, so 90° ÷ 2 = 45°. The 40 m does not matter.

subject: AM
q: The power output of an engine is 75 kW. How much energy, in megajoules, does it produce in one hour?
solution: Energy = power × time = 75,000 W × 3,600 s = 270,000,000 J. Divide by 1,000,000 to get megajoules. So the energy is 270 MJ.
trick: 75 kW for one hour is 75 kWh, and 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ. So 75 × 3.6 = 270 (75 × 3 = 225, plus 75 × 0.6 = 45).

subject: AM
q: What is the modulus of the complex number z = 11 + 60i?
solution: The modulus of a + bi is √(a² + b²). So |z| = √(11² + 60²) = √(121 + 3,600) = √3,721 = 61. The modulus is 61.
trick: Know the triple 11, 60, 61. Test it: (11² − 1) ÷ 2 = 120 ÷ 2 = 60, which matches the 60 given. When that matches, the hypotenuse is one more than the longer leg: 61.

subject: AM
q: Calculate the derivative of y = 5x³ at x = 1.
solution: By the power rule, y = 5x³ gives dy/dx = 5 × 3x² = 15x². At x = 1 this is 15 × 1² = 15. The derivative at x = 1 is 15.
trick: At x = 1, every power of x is 1, so the derivative is just coefficient × power: 5 × 3 = 15.

subject: AM
q: If y = 2x² + 4x, find dy/dx when x = 1.
solution: Differentiate term by term: 2x² gives 4x and 4x gives 4, so dy/dx = 4x + 4. At x = 1 that is 4 + 4 = 8. So dy/dx = 8.
trick: At x = 1, each term gives coefficient × power: 2 × 2 = 4 and 4 × 1 = 4. Add them to get 8.

subject: AM
q: If the probability of passing an exam is 0.7, what is the probability that exactly 3 students pass out of 4?
solution: This is a binomial with n = 4, p = 0.7 and 3 successes. P = C(4, 3) × 0.7³ × 0.3 = 4 × 0.343 × 0.3 = 0.4116. The probability is about 0.41.

subject: AM
q: Initial activity 320 mCi — 40 mCi after 18 hours. What is the half-life of the radioactive drug?
solution: From 320 mCi to 40 mCi is a drop by a factor of 320 ÷ 40 = 8 = 2³. So 3 half-lives passed in 18 hours. One half-life is 18 ÷ 3 = 6 hours.
trick: 320, 160, 80, 40 is three halvings. Split 18 hours into 3 equal parts: 6.

subject: AM
q: The theoretical yield of a reaction is 2,400g. If the percentage yield is 70%, what is the actual yield?
solution: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100, so actual = 70% of 2,400 = 0.7 × 2,400 = 1,680 g. The actual yield is 1,680 g.

subject: AM
q: The cost function is C(x) = 2x³ − 4x² + 10. What is the marginal cost at x = 2?
solution: Marginal cost is the derivative of the cost function: dC/dx = 6x² − 8x. At x = 2 that is 6 × 4 − 8 × 2 = 24 − 16 = 8. The marginal cost is 8.
trick: The constant 10 disappears. Write the derivative as 2x(3x − 4), which at x = 2 is 4 × 2 = 8.

subject: AM
q: Using the Newton-Raphson method to solve x² − 4 = 0, start with x₀ = 2.5. What is the next approximation?
solution: Newton-Raphson gives x₁ = x₀ − f(x₀) ÷ f′(x₀), with f(x) = x² − 4 and f′(x) = 2x. So x₁ = 2.5 − (6.25 − 4) ÷ 5 = 2.5 − 0.45 = 2.05. The next approximation is 2.05.
trick: For x² − a, Newton's step is the average of x₀ and a ÷ x₀. Here 4 ÷ 2.5 = 1.6, and the average of 2.5 and 1.6 is 2.05.

subject: AM
q: The velocity of a particle is v(t) = t³ − 6t. Find its acceleration at t = 2 s.
solution: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a = dv/dt = 3t² − 6. At t = 2 that is 3 × 4 − 6 = 12 − 6 = 6. The acceleration is 6 m/s².
trick: 3t² at t = 2 is 12, and the −6t term leaves −6. So 12 − 6 = 6.

subject: AM
q: A chemical reaction proceeds at a rate of 0.05 mol/L/s. The time to produce 2 moles in a 5L container is:
solution: Rate in the whole container = 0.05 mol/L/s × 5 L = 0.25 mol/s. Time for 2 mol = 2 ÷ 0.25 = 8 s. The time is 8 seconds.
trick: 0.25 mol per second is one mole every 4 seconds, so 2 moles take 8 seconds.

subject: AM
q: A vector has a magnitude of 25 and a direction of 90°. What is its vertical component?
solution: Vertical component = magnitude × sin θ, with θ measured from the horizontal axis. So it is 25 × sin 90° = 25 × 1 = 25. The vertical component is 25.
trick: 90° points straight up, so the whole vector is vertical: 25. The 0 option is the horizontal part, 25 cos 90°.

subject: AM
q: After flying 300km north and then 400km east, what is the straight-line distance from the start?
solution: North and east are at right angles, so the distance is the hypotenuse. d = √(300² + 400²) = √(90,000 + 160,000) = √250,000 = 500 km. The distance from the start is 500 km.
trick: 300 and 400 are 100 times 3 and 4, so this is the 3, 4, 5 triangle times 100: 500.

subject: AM
q: A vector is given by v = 5i − 12j. What is its magnitude?
solution: Magnitude = √(5² + (−12)²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The magnitude is 13 units.
trick: The minus sign does not matter because it gets squared. 5 and 12 make the 5, 12, 13 triangle, so 13.

subject: AM
q: The angle of depression from a 50m high cliff to a boat is 30°. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff?
solution: The angle of depression from the cliff top equals the angle of elevation from the boat, so tan 30° = 50 ÷ d. So d = 50 ÷ tan 30° = 50 ÷ (1/√3) = 50√3, which is about 86.6 m. The boat is 50√3 m from the base.
trick: tan 30° = 1/√3, so dividing by it just multiplies by √3: 50√3. The boat must be farther than 50 m (that is the 45° case), so the 50 m option is out.

subject: AM
q: Find the time t for the inflexion point in the rate function R(t) = 2t³ − 9t² + 12t + 1.
solution: An inflexion point is where the second derivative changes sign, so set it equal to 0. R′(t) = 6t² − 18t + 12, so R″(t) = 12t − 18. Setting 12t − 18 = 0 gives t = 18 ÷ 12 = 1.5. The inflexion point is at t = 1.5.
trick: For a cubic with terms at³ + bt², the inflexion is at t = −b ÷ (3a) = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5.

subject: AM
q: A civil engineer needs to create 4,500kg of concrete with a cement : sand : gravel ratio of 1:4:5. What mass of sand is required?
solution: The ratio 1 : 4 : 5 has 1 + 4 + 5 = 10 parts. Sand is 4 of the 10 parts, so its mass is 4/10 × 4,500 = 1,800 kg. The mass of sand is 1,800 kg.
trick: 10 parts means each part is 450 kg. Sand is 4 parts, so 4 × 450 = 1,800.

subject: AM
q: The density of lead is 11,300 kg/m³. Express this in g/cm³.
trick: Going from kg/m³ to g/cm³ always divides by 1,000 (water is 1,000 kg/m³ and 1 g/cm³). 11,300 ÷ 1,000 = 11.3.

subject: AM
q: The Newton-Raphson method is used to find a root of x² − 4 = 0. Starting with x₀ = 3, what is the value of x₁?
solution: Newton-Raphson gives x₁ = x₀ − f(x₀) ÷ f′(x₀), with f(x) = x² − 4 and f′(x) = 2x. So x₁ = 3 − (9 − 4) ÷ 6 = 3 − 5/6 = 13/6. The value of x₁ is 13/6.
trick: For x² − a, average x₀ and a ÷ x₀: (3 + 4/3) ÷ 2 = (13/3) ÷ 2 = 13/6. Also x₁ must be between 2 and 3, and only 13/6 is.

subject: AM
q: A rectangular pool has dimensions (x + 2) meters by x meters. If its perimeter is 48 meters, find x.
solution: Perimeter = 2((x + 2) + x) = 4x + 4. So 4x + 4 = 48, which gives x = 11 m.
trick: Half the perimeter is 24 = 2x + 2, so x = 11.

subject: AM
q: If a bag originally costs $30 and is on sale for 25% off, what is the cost price of 18 bags?
trick: 18 × 30 = 540, then take three quarters: 405.

subject: AM
q: The price of a gadget decreased by 20%. To restore the original price, by what percentage should the price be increased?
solution: After a 20% cut the price is 0.8 of the original. Getting back needs 1 ÷ 0.8 = 1.25 times the new price, a 25% increase.
trick: The cut over what is left: 20 ÷ 80 = 25%.

subject: AM
q: What is the volume in meters of a cubical silo with edges of a length of 5cm?
showNote: The show's bar wrote the unit as cm³; the volume is 125 cm³, which is 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
solution: The volume is 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³. One cubic metre is 10⁶ cm³, so 125 cm³ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

subject: AM
q: If Solution A has a molarity of 3/5 and Solution B has a molarity of 5/8, what is the ratio of Solution A to Solution B?
trick: Cross multiply: 3 × 8 to 5 × 5.

subject: AM
q: 75% of A's income is equal to 25% of B's income. The ratio of the incomes of A and B is
trick: Swap the percentages: 25 : 75 = 1 : 3.

subject: AM
q: A company has 150 employees. If each employee earns ₦500,000 per annum, what is the total annual salary of all employees?
trick: 150 × 500 = 75,000; three more zeros make 75 million.

subject: AM
q: In a lab, 50 mL of a 2 M solution is mixed with 10 mL of water. Find the resulting molarity.
showNote: The show's bar read 0.67 M or 2/3, but 0.1 mol in 60 mL is 5/3 ≈ 1.67 M.
solution: The amount of solute stays the same: 0.050 L × 2 M = 0.1 mol. The new volume is 60 mL, so the molarity is 0.1 ÷ 0.060 = 5/3 ≈ 1.67 M.
trick: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂: 2 × 50 = M₂ × 60, so M₂ = 100/60.

subject: AM
q: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for 12 cookies. How much flour is needed for 36 cookies?
solution: 36 cookies is 3 times 12, so the flour is 3 × 2 = 6 cups.

subject: AM
q: Machines A and B produce 30 and 45 units per hour, respectively. How long to produce 450 units together?
solution: Together they make 30 + 45 = 75 units an hour, so 450 ÷ 75 = 6 hours.

subject: AM
q: If vector Q = xi + yj + zk, what is the divergence of Q?
showNote: The show's bar read x + y + z; the divergence is ∂x/∂x + ∂y/∂y + ∂z/∂z = 3.
solution: Divergence adds the partial derivatives: ∂x/∂x + ∂y/∂y + ∂z/∂z = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.
trick: For the position vector in 3D, div r = 3.

subject: AM
q: What is the period if simple interest is ₦2,000, the principal is ₦10,000, and the rate is 8% per annum?

subject: AM
q: If the bearing from point X to point Y is N 60° E, what is the bearing from point Y to point X?
solution: N 60° E is a bearing of 060°. The bearing back adds 180°: 240°, which is S 60° W.
trick: Back bearing: add 180° (or subtract it if over 180°).

subject: AM
q: How many meters of rug 50cm wide will be required to cover the floor of a room 14m by 9m?
solution: Floor area = 14 × 9 = 126 m². A 0.5 m wide strip must be 126 ÷ 0.5 = 252 m long.
trick: Half a metre wide: double the area.

subject: AM
q: The sum of the eigenvalues of a square matrix is equal to its
solution: The sum of a square matrix's eigenvalues equals its trace, the sum of its diagonal entries. (Their product equals the determinant.)

subject: AM
q: How many different 3-letter combinations can be formed from the word ''MATH'"'?
showNote: This counts ordered arrangements (⁴P₃ = 24); unordered selections would be ⁴C₃ = 4.
solution: Choosing 3 of the 4 letters in order: ⁴P₃ = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 arrangements.

subject: AM
q: The Fourier series of an even function contains
solution: An even function has f(−x) = f(x), so all the sine terms vanish: the series has only cosine terms (and a constant).

subject: AM
q: A school's population decreased from 900 to 630 people. What is the percentage decrease in the population?

subject: AM
q: A circular well with a diameter of 2cm is dug to a depth of 14cm. What is the volume of the earth dug out?
solution: Radius 1 cm, depth 14 cm: V = πr²h = (22/7) × 1 × 14 = 44 cm³.

subject: AM
q: The Maclaurin series is a special case of the Taylor series at what value of x?
solution: A Maclaurin series is a Taylor series about x = 0.

subject: AM
q: The sides of a triangle are in a 2:3:5 ratio, and its perimeter is 96cm. The sum of the smallest and longest sides are
showNote: Sides in the ratio 2:3:5 cannot make a real triangle (2 + 3 = 5); the arithmetic still gives 67.2 cm.
solution: The parts total 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, so each part is 96 ÷ 10 = 9.6 cm. Smallest plus longest = (2 + 5) × 9.6 = 67.2 cm.

subject: AM
q: When is a vector field irrotational?
solution: A vector field F is irrotational when its curl is zero everywhere: ∇ × F = 0.

subject: AM
q: A microscope magnifies a virus from 4mm to 12mm. What is the percentage change in the magnification?
showNote: The show's bar read 2: the change as a fraction of the start, (12 − 4) ÷ 4 = 2, which is 200%.
solution: Change = 12 − 4 = 8 mm, and 8 ÷ 4 = 2, an increase of 200%.

subject: AM
q: If a bacteria population doubles every 3 hours, how long will it take to increase by a factor of 8?
solution: 8 = 2³, so it takes 3 doublings: 3 × 3 = 9 hours.

subject: AM
q: If the original price of an item is $250 and it is increased by 40%, what is the new price for 25 of these items?

subject: AM
q: If a shoe costs $60 and the seller offers a 10% discount on every 10 shoes purchased, how much is 20 shoes?
solution: 20 shoes cost 20 × $60 = $1,200 before the discount; 10% off gives $1,080.

subject: AM
q: A car rental company charges a base fee of N1,500 plus N250 per km. What is the cost of renting a car for 300 km?

subject: AM
q: In control systems, the state-space representation is written using
solution: State-space models write the system as first-order matrix equations, x′ = Ax + Bu and y = Cx + Du.

subject: AM
q: A bacteria population doubles every 4 hours. If there are initially 500 bacteria, how many will there be in 4 hours?
solution: 4 hours is one doubling period, so 500 becomes 1,000.

subject: AM
q: What is the area of a triangular garden that has a height of 10 meters and a base of 12 meters?
solution: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 12 × 10 = 60 m².

subject: AM
q: The number of ways in which 6 students can be seated in a line is
solution: 6 students in a line: 6! = 720 ways.

subject: AM
q: ₦15,000 invested at 6% simple interest grows to what amount in 4 years?
solution: Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100 = 15,000 × 6 × 4 ÷ 100 = ₦3,600. The amount is the principal plus the interest, so 15,000 + 3,600 = ₦18,600.
trick: Four years at 6% adds 24%, so the amount is 124% of 15,000. That is 15,000 + 3,000 (20%) + 600 (4%) = 18,600.

subject: AM
q: A pizza shop offers 10 toppings. How many 4-topping pizzas are possible?
solution: The order of toppings does not matter, so use combinations: 10C4 = (10 × 9 × 8 × 7) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 5,040 ÷ 24 = 210.
trick: Cancel before multiplying: 8 cancels with 4 × 2, and 9 cancels with 3, which leaves 10 × 3 × 7 = 210.

subject: AM
q: How many 5 letter words can be formed from ALPHA without repeating letters?
solution: ALPHA has 5 letters, and the letter A appears twice. Using every letter once, there are 5! = 120 orders, but swapping the two As gives the same word. So divide by 2!: 120 ÷ 2 = 60.
trick: 5! ÷ 2! is just 5 × 4 × 3, because the 2 × 1 cancels. That is 60.

subject: AM
q: If 64% show the dominant phenotype, find the recessive allele frequency (Hardy-Weinberg).
solution: The dominant phenotype covers p² + 2pq = 0.64, so the recessive phenotype is q² = 1 − 0.64 = 0.36. Check: q = 0.6 gives p = 0.4, and p² + 2pq = 0.16 + 0.48 = 0.64. So the recessive allele frequency is q = √0.36 = 0.6.
trick: Subtract from 100 first: 100 − 64 = 36, so q² = 0.36 and q = 0.6. Beware 0.4, which is the dominant allele p, not q.

subject: AM
q: How many distinct permutations can be made from “LEVEL”?
solution: LEVEL has 5 letters: L twice, E twice and V once. The number of distinct arrangements is 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30.
trick: L and E each appear twice, so halve 120 twice: 120 to 60 to 30. Stopping at 60 is the trap.

subject: AM
q: If 200 Joules of heat is added to a system that does 50 Joules of work, what is the internal energy change?
solution: First law of thermodynamics: ΔU = Q − W, where Q is heat added to the system and W is work done by the system. So ΔU = 200 − 50 = 150 J.
trick: 200 J goes in as heat and 50 J leaves as work, so 150 J stays inside.

subject: AM
q: An object appears as 12 millimetres on an image magnified 60 times. Determine the object's real size.
solution: Magnification = image size ÷ real size, so real size = image size ÷ magnification = 12 mm ÷ 60 = 0.2 mm.
trick: 12 ÷ 60 is one fifth, which is 0.2. The real object must be smaller than its enlarged image.

subject: AM
q: If you mix 200 millilitres of a 2.5 molar KCl solution with 300 millilitres of water, what is the final molarity of the solution?
solution: Use M₁V₁ = M₂V₂, taking the volumes to add. The final volume is 200 + 300 = 500 mL, so M₂ = 2.5 × 200 ÷ 500 = 1 M.
trick: The 200 mL is 2/5 of the final 500 mL, so the concentration falls to 2/5 of 2.5, which is 1 M.

subject: AM
q: A recessive disorder affects 1 in 2,500 people. What is the carrier frequency?
solution: For a recessive disorder, q² = 1 ÷ 2,500, so q = √(1 ÷ 2,500) = 1 ÷ 50 = 0.02. Carriers are 2pq = 2 × 0.98 × 0.02 = 0.0392. That is about 4%.
trick: √2,500 = 50, so q = 1 in 50, which is 2%. Carriers are about 2q = 4%, because p is almost 1.

subject: AM
q: From 4 red, 5 green, and 6 yellow marbles, how many ways can 3 marbles be chosen?
solution: The colours do not matter, so choose 3 from 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 marbles. 15C3 = (15 × 14 × 13) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 2,730 ÷ 6 = 455.
trick: Cancel first: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 and 14 ÷ 2 = 7, so the answer is 5 × 7 × 13 = 455.

subject: AM
q: After flying 300 kilometres north, then 400 kilometres east, determine the straight line distance between the starting and ending points.
solution: North and east are at right angles, so the distance is √(300² + 400²) = √(90,000 + 160,000) = √250,000 = 500 km.
trick: 300 and 400 are 3 and 4 scaled up by 100, so this is a 3, 4, 5 triangle and the distance is 500 km.

subject: AM
q: A pendulum has a period of 1.5 seconds. How many swings occur in 10 minutes?
solution: 10 minutes = 10 × 60 = 600 seconds. One swing takes one period, 1.5 seconds. So the number of swings is 600 ÷ 1.5 = 400.
trick: 1.5 seconds per swing means 2 swings every 3 seconds. 600 seconds holds 200 lots of 3 seconds, so 400 swings.

subject: AM
q: A 14,000 litres tank is 40% full. How many litres are needed to fill it to the brim?
solution: The tank is 40% full, so it needs the other 100% − 40% = 60% to be full. 60% of 14,000 = 0.6 × 14,000 = 8,400 litres.
trick: 10% of 14,000 is 1,400, so 60% is 6 × 1,400 = 8,400. The 5,600 option is the 40% already in the tank.

subject: AM
q: If the sum of two numbers is 150, and their difference is 30. Find the numbers?
solution: Let the numbers be x and y, with x + y = 150 and x − y = 30. Adding the equations gives 2x = 180, so x = 90, and then y = 150 − 90 = 60. The numbers are 90 and 60.
trick: Check the gaps in the options. 80 and 70 differ by 10, 100 and 50 differ by 50, and only 90 and 60 differ by 30.

subject: AM
q: The binary number 11010 is subtracted from 101101. What is the result in decimal?
trick: Read off the place values to get 45 and 26, then subtract: 45 − 26 = 19.

subject: AM
q: What is the heart rate of a person with an R-R interval of 80 seconds?
solution: Heart rate in beats per minute = 60 ÷ RR interval in seconds. So 60 ÷ 80 = 0.75 bpm.
trick: Beats per minute is 60 ÷ seconds per beat. 80 seconds per beat is slower than one beat a minute, so only 0.75 bpm fits.

subject: AM
q: What is the work done when a 10 Newton force moves an object through 15 metres?
solution: Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force = 10 N × 15 m = 150 J.
trick: Just multiply: 10 × 15 = 150. The other two options are half and double that.

subject: AM
q: What type of stress acts parallel to a surface?
solution: Axial and bulk stresses push or pull straight into a surface, at right angles to it. Stress that acts parallel to a surface, trying to slide one layer over the next, is shear stress.
trick: Parallel to the surface means sliding along it, and sliding is shear. The other two act straight into the surface.

subject: AM
q: The integral of cos(ax) dx is
solution: Let u = ax, so dx = du ÷ a. Then ∫cos(ax) dx = (1 ÷ a) ∫cos u du = (1 ÷ a) sin u + C. Putting u = ax back gives sin(ax)/a + C, so the answer is sin(ax)/a.
trick: Differentiating sin(ax) brings out a factor a, so integrating must divide by a to undo it. The options with a on top are wrong.

subject: AM
q: Divergence of a solenoidal field is
solution: A solenoidal field is defined as one with no sources or sinks, which means ∇·F = 0. The magnetic field B is the standard example. So its divergence is 0.
trick: Solenoidal means divergence free, so the answer is 0. Do not mix it up with irrotational, which means the curl is 0.

subject: AM
q: If a device draws 0.25 Ampere from a 120 Volt source, what is the resistance?
solution: Ohm's law: V = IR, so R = V ÷ I = 120 ÷ 0.25 = 480 Ω.
trick: 0.25 is a quarter, so dividing by 0.25 is the same as multiplying by 4: 120 × 4 = 480.

subject: AM
q: Given the position vector r(t) = (3t² − 4t)i + (2t³)j m, find the acceleration magnitude at t = 1 second
solution: Differentiate twice. The velocity is (6t − 4)i + 6t²j, so the acceleration is 6i + 12t j. At t = 1, a = 6i + 12j, so |a| = √(6² + 12²) = √180 = 6√5 m/s².
trick: At t = 1 the acceleration is 6i + 12j = 6(i + 2j), so its size is 6√(1 + 4) = 6√5. The j component alone is 12, which already rules out √5 and 3√5.

subject: AM
q: A rectangle has side lengths in a 3:4 ratio. If its perimeter is 56cm, what is its area?
solution: Let the sides be 3k and 4k. The perimeter is 2(3k + 4k) = 14k = 56, so k = 4. The sides are 12 cm and 16 cm, so the area is 12 × 16 = 192 cm².
trick: Half the perimeter is 28, shared 3 to 4 in 7 parts of 4 each. That gives sides 12 and 16, and 12 × 16 = 192.

subject: AM
q: The unit of thermal conductivity is
solution: Heat flow rate = k × area × temperature difference ÷ thickness, so k = W × m ÷ (m² × K) = W/(m·K). J/K is the unit of heat capacity and N·m is the unit of torque or energy. So the unit of thermal conductivity is W/mK.
trick: Thermal conductivity is watts per metre per kelvin, and W/mK is the only option with watts in it.

subject: AM
q: What is the unit of magnetic permeability?
solution: Permeability μ comes from B = μH, with B in tesla (Wb/m²) and H in A/m, so μ is in Wb/(A m). One henry is one weber per ampere, so the unit is Henry/meter.
trick: Weber is flux and the darcy is for rock, so only Henry/meter is left (and μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m).

subject: AM
q: ₦18,000 grows to ₦22,500 in 4 years with simple interest. What is the annual rate?
trick: The interest of 4,500 is a quarter of 18,000, which is 25% over 4 years, so 25 ÷ 4 = 6.25% a year.

subject: AM
q: The velocity of a particle is v(t) = 3t² − 12t. At what time t is the velocity zero?
solution: Set v = 0: 3t² − 12t = 3t(t − 4) = 0, so t = 0 (the start) or t = 4. Of the options, v(2) = −12 and v(6) = 36 are not zero. So the velocity is zero at t = 4 s.
trick: Cancel 3t from 3t² = 12t to leave t = 4 (t = 0 also works, but it is not offered).

subject: AM
q: The population P of bacteria grows at a rate dP/dt = 0.05P. If P₀ = 1000, what is the population after 20 hours?
solution: Growth at a rate proportional to P gives P = P₀ e^(kt). Here kt = 0.05 × 20 = 1, so P = 1,000 × e¹ = 1,000 × 2.718 ≈ 2,718.
trick: 0.05 × 20 = 1, so it is just 1,000 × e, and e ≈ 2.718 gives 2,718.

subject: AM
q: A 1,200 kilogram vehicle slows from 72 kilometres per hour to rest in 4 seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the average braking force.
solution: Convert the speed: 72 km/h = 72 ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s. The deceleration is a = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s², so F = ma = 1,200 × 5 = 6,000 N.

subject: AM
q: Rain chance per day = 0.6. The probability that it doesn't rain two days in a row is
solution: Read it as no rain on either of the two days. P(dry on one day) = 1 − 0.6 = 0.4, and the days are independent. So P(dry on both days) = 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16.
trick: Dry is 1 − 0.6 = 0.4, and 4 × 4 = 16, so 0.16. The option 0.4 is only one day, and 12 cannot be a probability.

subject: AM
q: If f(x) = 5x³ − 4x + 7, find f′(2)
solution: Differentiate term by term: f′(x) = 15x² − 4, because the constant 7 disappears. Then f′(2) = 15 × 4 − 4 = 60 − 4 = 56.
trick: The 7 vanishes, 5x³ gives 15x² and −4x gives −4. At x = 2 that is 60 − 4 = 56.

subject: AM
q: If a man's height is equal to the length of his shadow, what is the angle of elevation of the sun?
solution: The man, his shadow and the sun's ray form a right triangle with equal legs. So tan θ = height ÷ shadow = 1, which gives θ = 45°.
trick: Equal legs make an isosceles right triangle, so the angles are 45° each.

subject: AM
q: Which law relates current, voltage and resistance?
solution: Ohm's law, V = IR, ties together voltage, current and resistance. Pascal's law is about fluid pressure and Faraday's law is about induced voltage, so the answer is Ohm's law.
trick: V = IR has all three quantities, so it is Ohm's.

subject: AM
q: In fluid mechanics, the continuity equation ensures what?
showNote: The continuity equation states conservation of mass, so the option should read 'Mass conservation'. 'Mass concentration' is the mass of a substance per unit volume of a mixture, which is a different idea, but it is the only option about mass, so it is treated as the intended answer. The continuity equation expresses conservation of mass; the show's option reads 'Mass concentration'.
solution: The continuity equation expresses conservation of mass: for steady flow ρ₁A₁v₁ = ρ₂A₂v₂, so what flows in must flow out. The proper term is mass conservation, and the only option about mass is Mass concentration, so that is the answer.
trick: Continuity means conservation, mass in equals mass out, and only one option mentions mass.

subject: AM
q: An alloy of bronze is composed of copper and tin in a 4:6 ratio. To produce 150kg of bronze, what mass of tin is needed?
solution: Copper : tin = 4 : 6, so there are 4 + 6 = 10 parts in all and tin is 6 of them. Tin = 6/10 × 150 = 90 kg.
trick: One part is 150 ÷ 10 = 15 kg, so tin is 6 × 15 = 90.

subject: AM
q: A man borrowed ₦10,000 at 5% simple interest per annum. How much will he pay after 3 years?
solution: Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100 = 10,000 × 5 × 3 ÷ 100 = ₦1,500. He pays back the loan plus the interest: 10,000 + 1,500 = ₦11,500.
trick: Repayment must be more than the ₦10,000 borrowed, so only ₦11,500 can be right. Check: 5% is 500 a year, and 10,000 + 3 × 500 = 11,500.

subject: AM
q: What does the Jacobian represent in coordinate transformations?
solution: The Jacobian determinant tells you how much a small area or volume is stretched when you change coordinates, as in dx dy = r dr dθ for polar coordinates. So it is a scale factor.
trick: Think of polar coordinates, where the Jacobian r is the area stretch, so it is a scale factor.

subject: AM
q: Reynolds number identifies
solution: The Reynolds number Re = ρvD/μ compares inertial forces with viscous forces, and its size tells you whether flow is laminar or turbulent. So it identifies the flow regime.
trick: Re is the laminar versus turbulent number, which is the flow regime.

subject: AM
q: Divergence is a measure of what?
accept: net outward flux per unit volume
solution: Rotation is measured by the curl, not the divergence. Divergence ∇·F is the net outward flux per unit volume at a point, so it measures flux density.
trick: Divergence is flux out per unit volume, and curl is the one for rotation.

subject: AM
q: What type of stress occurs due to twisting?
solution: Compressive stress comes from pushing and tensile stress from pulling. Twisting a shaft produces shear stress across its section (τ = Tr/J), which is called torsional stress.
trick: Twisting is torsion, so the answer is torsional stress.

subject: AM
q: Find the eigenvalues of the matrix [[5, 2], [2, 5]].
solution: Solve det(A − λI) = (5 − λ)² − 2² = 0, so 5 − λ = ±2 and λ = 3 or 7. Check: 3 + 7 = 10 is the trace, and 3 × 7 = 21 is the determinant 25 − 4. The eigenvalues are 3 and 7.
trick: For a matrix [[a, b], [b, a]] the eigenvalues are a + b and a − b, so 5 + 2 = 7 and 5 − 2 = 3.

subject: AM
q: What is the divergence of a constant vector field?
solution: A constant field F = (a, b, c) has constant components, and divergence is ∂a/∂x + ∂b/∂y + ∂c/∂z, where every term is the derivative of a constant. So the divergence is 0.
trick: Divergence is a sum of derivatives, and the derivative of a constant is zero.

subject: AM
q: Which transform converts convolution to multiplication?
solution: The convolution theorem says the transform of a convolution equals the product of the two transforms, F(s) × G(s) for Laplace. The Fourier transform does this too, but it is not listed, so the answer is Laplace.
trick: Convolution theorem: only Laplace in this list turns convolution into a product.

subject: AM
q: A student mixes sand and cement in a ratio of 3:1. If he uses 9kg of sand, how much cement is required?
solution: Sand : cement = 3 : 1, so 3 parts of sand go with 1 part of cement. 9 kg of sand means each part is 9 ÷ 3 = 3 kg, so the cement needed is 3 kg.
trick: Divide the sand by 3: 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

subject: AM
q: When all eigenvalues are real, negative, and distinct, the system is
solution: For a linear system x′ = Ax, each mode behaves like e^(λt), so real negative eigenvalues make every mode die away to zero. That means the system is stable.
trick: Negative real eigenvalues mean everything decays, so it settles down: Stable.

subject: AM
q: A car travels 240 kilometres on 20 litres of petrol. How far, in kilometre, can it travel on 15 litres?
solution: The car does 240 ÷ 20 = 12 km per litre. On 15 litres it travels 12 × 15 = 180 km.
trick: 15 is three quarters of 20, so take three quarters of 240: 60 × 3 = 180.

subject: DA
q: In how many ways can 7 people be seated in a row if two of them insist on sitting next to each other?
solution: Treat the pair as one: 6! = 720 arrangements, times 2 for the pair's order: 1,440.

subject: DA
q: How many rectangles are there in a plane with 9 vertical and 9 horizontal lines?
solution: A rectangle needs 2 of the vertical lines and 2 of the horizontal ones: ⁹C₂ × ⁹C₂ = 36 × 36 = 1,296.

subject: DA
q: If you flip a fair coin three times, what is the probability of getting two heads in percentage?
solution: Exactly two heads: 3 of the 8 outcomes = 37.5%.

subject: DA
q: Seven persons are to be seated in a row. The probability that two particular persons sit next to each other is
solution: The pair sits together in 2 × 6! of the 7! orders: 2/7.

subject: DA
q: A couple has two children, and both are girls. What is the probability that their next child will be a boy?
solution: Each birth is independent of the earlier ones: 1/2.

subject: DA
q: A group of 5 people are randomly seated in a circle. What is the probability that 2 specific people sit next to each other in percentage?
showNote: The show's bar read 40%, which is the answer for 5 people in a row. Around a circle, the second person can be in 2 of the 4 seats left, next to the first: 50%.
solution: Fix one person; the other sits in one of the 4 remaining seats, 2 of which are next to the first: 2/4 = 50%.

subject: DA
q: A bag contains 5 green marbles, 4 blue marbles, and 3 red marbles. If two marbles are drawn at random, what is the probability that they are red?

subject: DA
q: If a study shows that 40 out of 200 people have a specific genetic trait, what is the probability that a randomly selected person from this group has the trait?

q: What is the product of 5 and the mean of the following dataset: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10?

q: How many ways can 8 people be arranged in a line?

q: How many ways can 5 books be arranged on a shelf?

subject: DA
q: A survey found that 60% of respondents prefer Product A. If 2,000 people were surveyed, how many did not prefer Product A?

subject: DA
q: Find the second quartile for the following set of numbers: 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 24.
solution: The second quartile is the median: the 6th of the 11 ordered values, 8.

subject: DA
q: When the mean of a group is 50 and variance is 64, find the coefficient of variation
solution: Standard deviation = √64 = 8, and CV = 8 ÷ 50 = 0.16 = 16%.

subject: DA
q: In a just concluded experiment, the quantity of salt particles in a solution is recorded as 5.6, 5.3, 5.2, 5.4, 5.7, 5.8. What is the average to one decimal place?

subject: DA

q: What is the probability of getting a sum of 3 if two dice are thrown?

subject: DA
q: A coin is flipped 10 times, and it lands heads up 8 times. What is the probability of it landing heads up on the next flip?
solution: Each flip of a fair coin is independent of the earlier ones: 1/2.

subject: DA
q: A city has 2 bus routes A and B. The probability of a bus being late on route A is 1/5, and route B is 1/2. What is the probability that at least one bus is late in percentage?
solution: Treating the routes as independent: 1 − (4/5 × 1/2) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6 = 60%.

subject: DA
q: A couple has five children, and all are girls. What is the probability that their next child will be a boy?
solution: Each birth is independent of the earlier ones: 1/2.

subject: DA
q: A company insures 1,000 cars. The probability of an accident in a year is 0.1. What is the expected number of accidents?

subject: DA
q: Four people each pick a number from 1 to 10. What's the chance that at least two people pick the same number?
solution: All different: 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 ÷ 10⁴ = 0.504, so at least two match: 1 − 0.504 = 0.496 = 49.6%.

subject: DA
q: If the probability of rain on any given day is 30%, what is the probability that it will rain at least once in 2 days in percentage?
solution: No rain on both days: 0.7 × 0.7 = 0.49, so rain at least once: 51%.

subject: DA
q: A medical study finds that 20% of people with a certain gene develop a disease. If 5% of the population has the gene, what is the probability of developing the disease in percentage?
showNote: This assumes only people with the gene develop the disease; 1% is the chance of having the gene and the disease.

subject: DA
q: If you roll two fair six-sided dice, what is the probability of rolling a sum greater than 9?
solution: Totals 10, 11 and 12 come up 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ways of 36: 1/6.

subject: DA
q: A deck of cards is shuffled. What is the probability of drawing a heart followed by a spade without replacement?

subject: DA
q: How many different ways can a president, vice-president, and secretary be chosen from a group of 10 people?

subject: DA
q: The quartiles, median, percentiles, and deciles are measures of central tendency classified as
solution: Quartiles, percentiles and deciles describe position in the ordered data, so they are called positional averages.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can 4 items be chosen from a set of 10?

subject: DA
q: The frequency distribution of exam scores is skewed to the right. Which measure of central tendency is likely to be the highest?
solution: A long right tail pulls the mean up past the median and the mode.

subject: DA
q: A store sells 250 units of a product per week. If the product costs ₦500 each, what is the total revenue for selling 200 products in a month?
solution: 200 × ₦500 = ₦100,000. (The 250 a week does not matter.)

subject: DA
q: What is the coefficient of variation of a sample that has a mean of 25 and standard deviation of 2?

subject: DA
q: Find the mean of the following numbers: 2.2, 10.2, 14.7, 5.9, 4.9, 11.1, 10.5

subject: DA
q: In how many ways can 3 students be chosen from a class of 12 students?

subject: DA
q: In a group of 200 people, 120 people own smartphones, and 140 people own laptops. If 80 people own both smartphones and laptops, how many people don't own either device?

subject: DA
q: In a dataset of 600 values, the 25th percentile is 20. How many values are below 20?

subject: DA
q: Two coins are flipped. What is the probability that both coins land on tails?

subject: DA
q: If the ratio of the mode to the median is 2:3 for a dataset, find the ratio of mode to mean.
solution: Mode ≈ 3 × median − 2 × mean. With mode 2 and median 3: 2 = 9 − 2 × mean, so mean = 3.5 and mode : mean = 2 : 3.5 = 4 : 7.

subject: DA
q: In a class of 30 students, 18 students play cricket, 15 students play football and 12 play both games. How many students in the class don't play either game?

subject: DA
q: In a sample of 1,000 voters, 540 voted for candidate A. What is the probability of a voter selecting candidate A in percentage?

subject: DA
q: If you have 12 different pairs of shoes, how many ways can you choose 8 pairs to wear today?
solution: The order of choosing does not matter, so use combinations. C(12, 8) = 12! ÷ (8! × 4!) = (12 × 11 × 10 × 9) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 11,880 ÷ 24 = 495. The answer is 495.
trick: Choosing 8 pairs to wear is the same as choosing 4 to leave out, so work out C(12, 4). Cancel as you go: 12 ÷ (4 × 3) = 1 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. That leaves 11 × 5 × 9 = 495.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can 5 players be arranged on a field?
solution: Each arrangement puts the 5 different players into 5 positions, so there are 5 choices for the first, 4 for the next, and so on. That gives 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. The answer is 120.
trick: Know the small factorials: 4! = 24, so 5! = 5 × 24 = 120.

subject: DA
q: In a heterozygote cross Aa x Aa, what is the probability of an offspring showing the dominant trait?
solution: Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, aA and aa, each equally likely. Only aa shows the recessive trait, so the other 3 of the 4 outcomes show the dominant trait (assuming complete dominance). The probability is 3/4.
trick: Only aa misses the dominant trait, and that is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. So 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

subject: DA
q: Find the interest accrued on a $18,000 loan at 4.5% simple interest for 2 years.
solution: Simple interest I = P × R × T = 18,000 × 0.045 × 2 = 1,620. The interest accrued is $1,620.
trick: 4.5% a year for 2 years is 9% of the loan. 10% of 18,000 is 1,800 and 1% is 180, so 9% is 1,800 − 180 = 1,620.

subject: DA
q: If the mean of a dataset is 40, the median is 50, and the mode is 60, what type of skewness does the distribution have?
solution: Here the mean (40) is below the median (50), which is below the mode (60). Pearson's coefficient of skewness is (mean − mode) ÷ SD = (40 − 60) ÷ SD, which is negative. So the long tail is on the left and the skewness is negative.
trick: Mean minus mode is 40 − 60 = −20, which is below zero, so the skew is negative.

subject: DA
q: What is the probability of selecting an even number between 1 and 20?
solution: From 1 to 20 there are 20 whole numbers and 10 of them are even. So P(even) = 10 ÷ 20 = 1/2. If 1 and 20 are left out, it is 9 even out of 18, which is still 1/2. The answer is 1/2.
trick: Odd and even numbers alternate, and there is an even count of numbers here, so exactly half are even: 1/2.

subject: DA
q: For data X: 5, 10, 15; Y: 15, 10, 5, find the correlation coefficient.
solution: Each time X goes up by 5, Y goes down by 5, so Y = 20 − X exactly. All the points lie on one straight line sloping down. So the correlation coefficient is r = −1.
trick: Y is exactly 20 − X, a perfect downhill line, so r = −1 with no working.

subject: DA
q: In a group of 60, 35 like music, 30 like sports, 20 like both. How many like neither?
solution: The number who like at least one = 35 + 30 − 20 = 45, because the 20 who like both were counted twice. So the number who like neither = 60 − 45 = 15. The answer is 15.
trick: Neither = total − A − B + both = 60 − 35 − 30 + 20 = 15.

subject: DA
q: A line graph is best suited to represent ____ data
solution: A line graph joins points in order along the horizontal axis, so it shows how a value changes over time. Data recorded over time is called time-series data.
trick: Line graph means change over time, so the word is time-series.

subject: DA
q: A normal distribution has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. What proportion of data lies between 40 and 60?
solution: 40 and 60 are 1 SD below and above the mean (50 ± 10). By the empirical rule, about 68% of the data lies within 1 SD of the mean. The answer is 68% (more exactly 68.27%).
trick: 40 to 60 is the mean ± 1 SD, and for a normal distribution that always holds about 68%.

subject: DA
q: A coin is tossed 7 times. What is the probability of getting heads all 7 times?
solution: The tosses are independent, so P(7 heads) = (1/2)⁷ = 1/128. The answer is 1/128.
trick: It is 1 over 2⁷. Double 2 six more times: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. So 1/128.

subject: DA
q: In a discrete uniform distribution on {1, 2,..., 9}, find its mean.
solution: For a discrete uniform distribution on 1 to 9, the mean is the average of the smallest and largest values: (1 + 9) ÷ 2 = 5. Check: the sum is 45 and 45 ÷ 9 = 5. The answer is 5.
trick: The values are evenly spaced, so the mean is the middle one, 5.

subject: DA
q: In a dataset of 20 values arranged in ascending order, Q1 is located at the
showNote: The position of Q1 depends on the quartile rule, and the question names none. The n ÷ 4 rule gives the 5th value, which is the show's answer, but the (n + 1) ÷ 4 rule gives 5.25 (a quarter of the way from the 5th to the 6th value), and the median of the lower half is the average of the 5th and 6th values. With the (n + 1) ÷ 4 rule, Q1 sits at position 5.25, a quarter of the way from the 5th to the 6th value. The show used n ÷ 4 = 5.
solution: With the n ÷ 4 rule, the position of Q1 is 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so Q1 is at the 5th value. Some books use (n + 1) ÷ 4 = 21 ÷ 4 = 5.25 instead, which is a quarter of the way from the 5th to the 6th value. So the question can be read two ways, but the expected answer is the 5th value.
trick: Take a quarter of the 20 values: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so the 5th value.

subject: DA
q: A normal distribution has a mean of 84 and a standard deviation of 32. Find the z-score for 100.
trick: The gap is 100 − 84 = 16, which is half of 32. So z = 0.5.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can 8 pairs of shoes be selected from 12 distinct pairs?
solution: Order does not matter, so use combinations. C(12, 8) = C(12, 4) = (12 × 11 × 10 × 9) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 11,880 ÷ 24 = 495.
trick: Choosing 8 means leaving out 4, so use C(12, 4). Cancel as you go: 12 ÷ (4 × 3) = 1 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5, leaving 11 × 5 × 9 = 495.

subject: DA
q: What is the Z-score of a student who scored 85 in a test with mean 78 and standard deviation 4?
trick: 7 ÷ 4 is just under 2, since 8 ÷ 4 would be 2. Only 1.75 is below 2, so pick it without dividing.

subject: DA
q: In a school of 150 students, 100 take French, 60 take Arabic, and 20 take neither. How many take both?
solution: The students taking at least one language number 150 − 20 = 130. Using total = French + Arabic − both, 130 = 100 + 60 − both. So both = 160 − 130 = 30.
trick: The two class lists add to 100 + 60 = 160, but only 150 − 20 = 130 students take a language. The extra 30 are the students counted twice.

subject: DA
q: Given the data points: 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Calculate the new mean if the smallest value is excluded.
solution: With 8 left out, the data are 11, 14, 17, 20. The sum is 62 and there are 4 values, so the mean is 62 ÷ 4 = 15.5. The answer is 15.5.
trick: The four numbers rise by 3 each time, so the mean is halfway between the first and last: (11 + 20) ÷ 2 = 15.5.

subject: DA
q: A jar has 48 red and black marbles. If the probability of drawing a black marble is 3/4, how many red marbles are there?
solution: Black marbles = 3/4 × 48 = 36. So red marbles = 48 − 36 = 12. The answer is 12.
trick: If black is 3/4 of the jar, red is 1/4. And 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

subject: DA
q: A pizza shop has 6 toppings. How many 3-topping pizzas are possible?
solution: The order of the toppings does not matter, so use combinations. C(6, 3) = (6 × 5 × 4) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 120 ÷ 6 = 20. The answer is 20 pizzas.
trick: In (6 × 5 × 4) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1), the 6 on top cancels the whole bottom (3 × 2 × 1 = 6), leaving 5 × 4 = 20.

subject: DA
q: In a class of 60 students, 40 study CHM 101, 30 PHY 101, and 20 both. How many students study only CHM 101?
solution: The students who study only CHM 101 are those in CHM 101 who are not also in PHY 101. So only CHM 101 = 40 − 20 = 20. The answer is 20.
trick: Only CHM = all CHM minus those who also take PHY: 40 − 20 = 20. The 10 option is the number who study only PHY 101 (30 − 20).

subject: DA
q: If the probability of hitting a target is 0.3, find the variance.
showNote: For a single shot (a Bernoulli trial) the variance is p(1 − p) = 0.3 × 0.7 = 0.21.
solution: For a single shot (a Bernoulli trial) with p = 0.3, the variance is p(1 − p) = 0.3 × 0.7 = 0.21. The answer is 0.21.
trick: p(1 − p) = 0.3 × 0.7, and 3 × 7 = 21 with two decimal places gives 0.21.

subject: DA
q: The variable that assigns a real number value to an event in a sample space is called a ____ variable
solution: A variable that assigns a real number to each outcome in a sample space is the definition of a random variable. Its value depends on the chance outcome. So the missing word is random.
trick: Random variable is the standard probability term. Static and defined are not used for this.

subject: DA
q: Given that the hours studied per week by 4 students are 5, 7, 18, and 30, calculate the interquartile range.
solution: Put the data in order: 5, 7, 18, 30. Taking the median of each half, Q1 = (5 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6 and Q3 = (18 + 30) ÷ 2 = 24. So IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 24 − 6 = 18. The answer is 18.
trick: Half the top pair minus half the bottom pair: (18 + 30 − 5 − 7) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18.

subject: DA
q: Form a committee of 3 men and 2 women from 8 men and 6 women. How many committees are possible?
solution: Choose the men and the women separately, then multiply. C(8, 3) = (8 × 7 × 6) ÷ 6 = 56 and C(6, 2) = (6 × 5) ÷ 2 = 15. So the number of committees = 56 × 15 = 840. The answer is 840.
trick: C(8, 3) = 56 and C(6, 2) = 15. Halve one and double the other: 56 × 15 = 28 × 30 = 840.

subject: DA
q: Find the 40th percentile of the data: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
solution: There are 6 values, so the 40th percentile is at position 0.4 × (6 + 1) = 2.8. That is 0.8 of the way from the 2nd value (10) to the 3rd value (15). So P40 = 10 + 0.8 × 5 = 14. The answer is 14.
trick: Position 0.4 × 7 = 2.8, so the answer lies between the 2nd and 3rd values, 10 and 15, and only 14 fits. For the exact value go 4/5 of the way up: 10 + 4 = 14.

subject: DA
q: The mean is 40 and the median is 35. The distribution is
showNote: A mean above the median points to a positive (right) skew. None of the options shown is right; the show's answer bar said Symmetrical.
solution: The mean (40) is above the median (35), so a long tail on the right is pulling the mean up. That is a positive (right) skew. A symmetrical or zero skew distribution has the mean equal to the median, and a negative skew has the mean below the median. None of the three options shows it, but the correct answer is positively skewed.
trick: Compare mean with median. Mean above median means positive skew, below means negative, and equal means symmetrical. Here 40 is above 35, so positive.

subject: DA
q: In a class of 4 Science, 5 Art, and 6 Medicine students, what is the probability that if 3 are picked, they are all Art?
solution: There are 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 students, and 5 of them are Art. P(all 3 are Art) = C(5, 3) ÷ C(15, 3) = 10 ÷ 455 = 2/91. The answer is 2/91.
trick: Multiply draw by draw: 5/15 × 4/14 × 3/13 = 1/3 × 2/7 × 3/13. The 3s cancel, leaving 2/(7 × 13) = 2/91.

subject: DA
q: How many SD above the mean is a 4-week project, given that the mean is 4 weeks and the SD is 0.5?
solution: z = (x − mean) ÷ SD = (4 − 4) ÷ 0.5 = 0. So a 4-week project is 0 SD above the mean. The answer is 0.
trick: 4 weeks is exactly the mean, so there is no gap and the answer is 0.

subject: DA
q: If three unbiased coins are tossed, what is the probability of getting two heads?
solution: Exactly two heads: HHT, HTH and THH, 3 of the 8 outcomes.

subject: DA
q: If three unbiased coins are tossed, what is the probability of getting at least two heads?
solution: Two or three heads: 3 + 1 = 4 of the 8 outcomes, 1/2.

subject: DA
q: Two unbiased coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at most 1 head?
solution: 0 or 1 head: TT, HT and TH, 3 of the 4 outcomes.

subject: DA
q: In a survey, 70% of respondents liked chocolate, and 60% liked vanilla. What is the percentage of respondents who like both flavors?
showNote: This assumes every respondent liked at least one of the two flavours.

subject: DA
q: A coin is tossed. What is the total probability of all the possible outcomes?
solution: The probabilities of all the outcomes always add up to 1.

subject: DA
q: A student scored 75, 85, 90, 95, and 105 on five tests. What is the product of the mean score and itself?
showNote: The show said "four tests", but five scores are listed.

subject: DA
q: How many different 5-letter words can be formed using the letters in the word "BATTLE"?
solution: BATTLE has two Ts. Using both Ts: choose 3 of B, A, L, E (4 ways) and arrange, 4 × 5!/2! = 240. Using at most one T: arrange 5 different letters, 5! = 120. Total 360.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can 5 books be selected from a shelf of 8 books?
solution: ⁸C₅ = ⁸C₃ = 56.

subject: DA
q: A survey of 100 students found that 60 like pizza, 40 like burgers, and 20 like both. Calculate the probability of a student liking pizza or burgers.

subject: DA
q: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by skewness?
solution: The mean is pulled toward the long tail, so it is the measure most affected.

subject: DA
q: How many combinations of 4 items can be chosen from 11 items?

subject: DA
q: A mathematics teacher calculated a test score as 102. The mean is 144 and the standard deviation is 21. Find the z-score.

subject: DA
q: The following sizes of clothes were sold in a day: 5, 8, 9, 5, 6, 4, 9, 3, 9, 3, 6. Calculate the mode.
solution: 9 appears three times, more than any other size.

subject: DA
q: In a survey of 90 people, 55 like tea, and 40 like coffee. If 20 people like both beverages, how many people don't like either?
solution: Tea or coffee: 55 + 40 − 20 = 75, so 90 − 75 = 15 like neither.

subject: DA
q: In how many ways can we paint the 6 faces of a cube with 6 different colours?
solution: 6! = 720 ways to place the colours, but each colouring can be turned 24 ways: 720 ÷ 24 = 30.

subject: DA
q: What is the probability that both the husband and his wife will be selected for an interview, given their probabilities of being selected are 1/7 and 1/5 respectively?

subject: DA
q: From a pack of 52 cards, one card is drawn at random. What is the probability that the card drawn is a ten or a spade?
solution: 13 spades plus the 3 other tens: 16 of 52 = 4/13.

subject: DA
q: Two dice are tossed. The probability that a total score is a prime number is
solution: Prime totals 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 come up 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15 ways of 36: 5/12.

subject: DA
q: If the probability of event A is 0.7 and the probability of event B is 0.6, what is the probability of both events A and B occurring?
showNote: This assumes A and B are independent.

subject: DA
q: A box contains 20 electric bulbs, out of which 4 are defective. One bulb is chosen at random from this box. What is the probability of getting a defective bulb?

subject: DA
q: A student guesses the answers to 5 true or false questions. If each question has exactly one correct answer, what is the probability of getting all 5 correct?

subject: DA
q: A speaks the truth in 75% of cases and B in 80% of the cases. In what percentage of cases are they likely to contradict each other, narrating the same incident?
showNote: The show's bar read 16%. They contradict each other when exactly one of them tells the truth: 0.75 × 0.2 + 0.25 × 0.8 = 0.35.
solution: P(A true, B false) + P(A false, B true) = 0.15 + 0.20 = 0.35 = 35%.

subject: DA
q: A fair coin is tossed till a head appears for the first time. The probability that the number of required tosses is odd is?

subject: DA
q: What is the z-score of a data point with a value of 50 in a dataset with a mean of 40 and a standard deviation of 5?

subject: DA
q: A bag contains 7 red balls and 5 blue balls. If three balls are drawn without replacement, what's the probability they're all red?

subject: DA
q: If 5 books are to be selected from a shelf of 10 books, how many different selections are possible?
solution: ¹⁰C₅ = 252.

subject: DA
q: How many different committees can be formed from a group of 9 people?
showNote: 512 = 2⁹ counts every possible group, including the empty one; if a committee must have at least one person, the answer is 511.
solution: Each person is either in or out: 2⁹ = 512.

subject: DA
q: In an exam, 60% of students scored below 75 marks. What is the percentile rank of a student who scored 75?
solution: Percentile rank is the percentage of scores that lie below a given score. Here 60% of the students scored below 75, so a score of 75 has a percentile rank of 60. The answer is 60, the 60th percentile.
trick: The question already says 60% scored below 75, and that percentage is the percentile rank. So just say 60.

subject: DA
q: Pie chart allocations: Education 10%, Health 20%, Infrastructure 20%. What angle represents the remaining sectors?
solution: The listed sectors add up to 10% + 20% + 20% = 50%, so the remaining sectors are 100% − 50% = 50% of the chart. A full circle is 360°, so the angle is 50% × 360° = 180°. The answer is 180°.
trick: The three shares make 50%, which is half the pie. Half of 360° is 180°.

subject: DA
q: Find the z-score for x = 17 if the mean = 15 and the standard deviation σ = 2.
solution: z = (x − mean) ÷ σ = (17 − 15) ÷ 2 = 2 ÷ 2 = 1. The answer is 1.
trick: 17 is 2 above the mean of 15, and the SD is 2. One SD above the mean means z = 1.

subject: DA
q: A bar graph shows Company X's profit is 150% of Company Y's. If Y's profit is ₦200,000, what is X's?
solution: X's profit is 150% of Y's, so X = 1.5 × ₦200,000 = ₦300,000. The answer is ₦300,000.
trick: 150% means the whole plus half. Half of 200,000 is 100,000, so 200,000 + 100,000 = 300,000.

subject: DA
q: In a normal distribution, mean = 50, SD = 5. What percentage lies between 45 and 55?
solution: The mean is 50 and the SD is 5, so 45 and 55 are exactly one SD below and above the mean. In a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within one SD of the mean. The answer is 68%.
trick: 45 to 55 is the mean ± 1 SD. Use the 68, 95, 99.7 rule, so the answer is 68%.

subject: DA
q: A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue, and 3 green balls. If 2 are drawn without replacement, what's the chance both are red?
solution: There are 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 balls. P(first red) = 4/12, and P(second red) = 3/11 because one red ball has gone. So P(both red) = 4/12 × 3/11 = 12/132 = 1/11. The answer is 1/11.
trick: Multiply the tops and the bottoms: (4 × 3) ÷ (12 × 11). The 4 × 3 = 12 cancels the 12 on the bottom, leaving 1/11.

subject: DA
q: A dataset has Q1 = 15 and Q3 = 45. Calculate the lower outlier threshold using the 1.5 × IQR rule.
showNote: Q1 − 1.5 × IQR = 15 − 1.5 × 30 = −30. The show's answer bar said 30, which drops the minus sign.
solution: The lower fence is Q1 − 1.5 × IQR. IQR = 45 − 15 = 30, so the fence is 15 − 1.5 × 30 = 15 − 45 = −30. The show's 30 has lost its minus sign. The answer is −30.
trick: IQR is 30 and 1.5 × 30 = 45. Then 15 − 45 = −30, so keep the minus sign.

subject: DA
q: If r = 0.78 for study hours vs exam scores, what percentage of correlation is implied?
showNote: The wording 'percentage of correlation' is loose. Read as the strength of the correlation, r = 0.78 gives 78%, which is the show's answer. Read as the share of variation in scores explained by study hours, it is r² ≈ 61%. The show read r = 0.78 as 78%. The share of the variation in scores that study hours explain is r² ≈ 61%.
solution: Here r = 0.78, so the correlation is positive and fairly strong, and read as a percentage it is 78%. Strictly, the share of the variation in scores explained by study hours is r² = 0.78² ≈ 0.61, or 61%. The question asks for the percentage of correlation, so the answer is 78%.
trick: Just turn 0.78 into 78%. Square r only when the question says variation explained.

subject: DA
q: A histogram bin (20-30) has frequency 15 in 150 observations. What is its relative frequency?
solution: Relative frequency = frequency ÷ total observations = 15 ÷ 150 = 0.1. As a percentage that is 10%. The answer is 10%.
trick: 15 out of 150 is 1 out of 10, which is 10%.

subject: DA
q: How many ways can 5 trophies be arranged in a display case?
solution: Five different trophies in a row can be arranged in 5! ways. 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. The answer is 120.

subject: DA
q: In a survey, 40% like Tea, 30% like Coffee, and 10% like both. What percentage likes neither?
solution: People who like Tea or Coffee: 40% + 30% − 10% = 60%, because the 10% who like both were counted twice. Those who like neither are 100% − 60% = 40%. The answer is 40%.
trick: 40 + 30 = 70, minus the 10 counted twice gives 60. Then 100 − 60 = 40.

subject: DA
q: A scatterplot shows data points forming a perfect downward straight line. What is the correlation coefficient?
solution: A perfect straight line means the correlation coefficient has size 1. A downward line means the relationship is negative, so r = −1. The answer is −1.
trick: Perfect means 1 in size and downward means negative, so −1.

subject: DA
q: A regression line has equation y = 1.2x + 5. Estimate y when x = 10.
solution: Put x = 10 into y = 1.2x + 5. That gives y = 1.2 × 10 + 5 = 12 + 5 = 17. The answer is 17.
trick: 1.2 × 10 is 12 (just move the decimal point), and 12 + 5 = 17.

subject: DA
q: A factory's output has mean 100, median 95, mode 90. What is the distribution's skew direction?
solution: Here the mean (100) is above the median (95), which is above the mode (90). The mean is pulled towards the long tail, so the tail is on the high side. That is a right (positive) skew. The answer is right skewed.
trick: The mean is the biggest of the three, so the tail points up the number line to the right. Right skewed.

subject: DA
q: Four fair coins are flipped. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
solution: It is easier to use the complement. P(no heads) = P(all four tails) = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. So P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16. The answer is 15/16.
trick: The only way to get no heads is all tails, which is 1 out of 16 outcomes. So the answer is 15 out of 16.

subject: DA
q: If a drawn marble is red from 4 red & 6 blue, what's P(next is blue without replacement)?
solution: The first marble was red and is not put back, so 3 red and 6 blue marbles remain, 9 in all. P(next is blue) = 6/9 = 2/3. The answer is 6/9, which equals 2/3.
trick: Removing a red leaves the 6 blue untouched but cuts the total to 9. So it is 6/9 straight away.

subject: DA
q: A data set of 10 values is arranged in ascending order. The 70th percentile corresponds to which value's position?
showNote: The position depends on the percentile rule, and the question names none. The (n + 1) rule gives 0.7 × 11 = 7.7, which is the show's answer, but the nearest rank rule gives 0.7 × 10 = 7, the 7th value, and that is also an option.
solution: One common rule puts the P-th percentile at position P/100 × (n + 1). Here that is 70/100 × (10 + 1) = 0.7 × 11 = 7.7. So the 70th percentile sits 0.7 of the way from the 7th value to the 8th value. The answer is the 7.7th value.

subject: DA
q: In a pie chart, a sector representing 55% of the data would have a central angle of how many degrees?
solution: A sector's central angle is its share of 360°. For 55%, the angle is 55% × 360° = 0.55 × 360° = 198°. The answer is 198°.

subject: DA
q: Aryan borrowed ₦2,000 at 5% per annum simple interest. Find the interest he will pay after 3 years.
trick: 5% of ₦2,000 is ₦100 for one year. Three years is ₦300.

subject: DA
q: In a dataset, X = {2, 4, 6, 8}, Y = {1, 3, 5, 7}. The population covariance between X and Y is:
solution: The deviations from the mean are −3, −1, 1, 3 for both X (mean 5) and Y (mean 4). Population covariance = Σ(dx × dy) ÷ n = (9 + 1 + 1 + 9) ÷ 4 = 20 ÷ 4 = 5. The answer is 5.
trick: Y is just X − 1, so the covariance equals the variance of X. The deviations of X from its mean 5 are −3, −1, 1, 3, so the variance is (9 + 1 + 1 + 9) ÷ 4 = 5.

subject: DA
q: If a bar graph has unequal bar widths, which adjustment must be made?
solution: When the bars have unequal widths (a histogram with unequal class widths), a wide bar looks bigger even if it holds few values. So divide each frequency by its class width to get the frequency density, and plot that. Then the area of each bar stands for its frequency. The answer is use frequency density.
trick: Unequal widths means height alone misleads, so divide by the width. Frequency ÷ width is frequency density.

subject: DA
q: If Q1 = 10, Q3 = 30, what is the upper outlier threshold?
solution: Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5 × IQR. IQR = 30 − 10 = 20, so the fence is 30 + 1.5 × 20 = 30 + 30 = 60. The answer is 60.
trick: IQR is 20 and 1.5 × 20 = 30. Add that to Q3: 30 + 30 = 60.

subject: DA
q: A 4-digit ATM PIN is chosen from 0 to 9. How many possible PINs exist?
solution: Each of the 4 places can hold any of the 10 digits from 0 to 9, and digits can repeat in a PIN. So the number of PINs is 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10⁴ = 10,000. The answer is 10,000.
trick: Four places with 10 choices each: write 1 followed by four zeros, 10,000.

subject: DA
q: The probability of passing Math is 0.25 and English is 0.5. If independent, what is the chance of passing both?
solution: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.25 × 0.5 = 0.125. The answer is 0.125.
trick: 0.5 is a half, so just halve 0.25 to get 0.125.

subject: DA
q: Calculate the coefficient of variation for a distribution with a mean of 150 and a standard deviation of 225.
solution: Coefficient of variation = SD ÷ mean = 225 ÷ 150 = 1.5. As a percentage that is 1.5 × 100 = 150%. The answer is 1.5 or 150%.
trick: 225 is 150 plus half of 150, so the ratio is 1.5. That is 150%.

subject: DA
q: A uniform distribution ranges from 10 to 30. What is the probability of X less than 15?
solution: For a uniform distribution from 10 to 30, P(X < 15) = (15 − 10) ÷ (30 − 10) = 5 ÷ 20 = 1/4. The answer is 1/4.
trick: The full range is 20 wide, and the part below 15 is 5 wide. So 5 out of 20 is 1/4.

subject: DA
q: In a race with 10 athletes, how many ways can gold, silver, and bronze be awarded?
solution: Gold, silver and bronze are different places, so order matters. There are 10 choices for gold, then 9 for silver, then 8 for bronze: 10 × 9 × 8 = 720. The answer is 720.
trick: Multiply three descending numbers from 10: 10 × 9 = 90, then 90 × 8 = 720.

subject: DA
q: If the mean is less than the median in a dataset, what does this indicate?
solution: The mean is pulled towards the tail of a distribution, so a mean below the median points to a long tail on the left. That is negative skew. The answer is negative skew.
trick: Mean below median means the tail is dragged to the left, so negative skew. Mean above median would be positive.

subject: DA
q: How many length-10 strings over the alphabet {A,B,C} contain exactly four A’s?
solution: Choose which 4 of the 10 places hold an A: C(10, 4) = 210 ways. Each of the other 6 places is B or C, so there are 2⁶ = 64 ways. Multiply: 210 × 64 = 13,440. The answer is 13,440.
trick: All strings number 3¹⁰ = 59,049, and ours are only some of them, so the count must be below 59,049. That rules out 153,090 and 59,049, leaving 13,440.

subject: DA
q: If mean = 100, SD = 15, what is the z-score of X = 115?
trick: 115 is exactly 15 above the mean, and the SD is 15. That is one SD up, so z = 1.

subject: DA
q: What is the average of 15, 25, 35, and 45?
solution: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = (15 + 25 + 35 + 45) ÷ 4 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30.
trick: The numbers go up in equal steps, so the mean is the middle point, halfway between 25 and 35, which is 30.

subject: DA
q: Calculate the probability that the sum of two dice is 9.
solution: Two dice give 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes. A sum of 9 comes from (3, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4) and (6, 3), which is 4 outcomes. So P = 4/36 = 1/9.
trick: A sum of 7 has the most ways, 6. Every step away from 7 loses one way, so 9 has 6 − 2 = 4 ways, and 4/36 = 1/9.

subject: DA
q: A survey asks 8 questions with 3 possible answers each. How many possible responses are there?
solution: Each of the 8 questions has 3 possible answers, and the choices are independent, so the total is 3⁸. Since 3⁴ = 81, 3⁸ = 81² = 6,561.
trick: Powers of 3 end in 3, 9, 7, 1 and repeat every 4 steps. 8 is a multiple of 4, so 3⁸ ends in 1, and only 6,561 does.

subject: DA
q: If X increases and Y decreases, correlation is:
solution: Correlation measures how two variables move together. When X goes up and Y goes down, they move in opposite directions, so the correlation is negative.
trick: Opposite directions means a negative sign. Same direction is positive, and no pattern at all is zero.

subject: DA
q: Given mean = 80, median = 85, SD = 5, find the coefficient of skewness.
showNote: This is Pearson's second coefficient, 3(mean − median) ÷ SD = −3; (mean − median) ÷ SD alone would give −1.
solution: With the median given, use Pearson's second coefficient of skewness: 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD. The mean is below the median, so the answer is negative. 3 × (80 − 85) ÷ 5 = 3 × (−5) ÷ 5 = −3.
trick: Mean minus median is −5 and the SD is 5, so they cancel to −1. Then multiply by 3 to get −3.

subject: DA
q: A dataset has values: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. What is the variance?
showNote: This is the population variance (divide by 5); dividing by 4 for a sample gives 250, also an option.
solution: Mean = 150 ÷ 5 = 30. The squared deviations are 400, 100, 0, 100 and 400, which add up to 1000. Treat the list as the whole dataset and divide by n = 5 (dividing by 4 would give the sample variance, 250). Variance = 1000 ÷ 5 = 200.
trick: For evenly spaced values, the population variance is step² × (n² − 1) ÷ 12. Here that is 10² × 24 ÷ 12 = 100 × 2 = 200.

subject: DA
q: A dataset of 9 exam scores: 55, 60, 65, 85, 90, 95. What is the first quartile?
showNote: The stem says 9 exam scores but lists only six, so the data is incomplete as worded. Using the six shown, Q1 = 60 (median of the lower half), which matches the show's answer; other quartile methods give 58.75 or 61.25, and 60 is the nearest option either way. Only six scores are listed; the median of their lower half (55, 60, 65) is 60.
solution: The question says 9 scores but lists only six, so use the six shown: 55, 60, 65, 85, 90, 95. Split them into a lower half (55, 60, 65) and an upper half (85, 90, 95). The first quartile is the median of the lower half, so Q1 = 60.
trick: Q1 is the middle of the bottom half. The bottom three are 55, 60, 65, so Q1 is 60. The 30 is below every score, and 65 is the top of the bottom half, not its middle.

subject: DA
solution: The multiplication rule says P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B | A). So P(A ∩ B) = 0.8 × 0.4 = 0.32. The value P(B) = 0.5 is not needed.
trick: Multiply 8 × 4 = 32, then give it two decimal places: 0.32. P(B) is a decoy.

subject: DA
q: Find the mean of 6, 9, 12, 15, 18.
trick: The numbers go up in equal steps of 3, so the mean is the middle number, 12. No adding is needed.

subject: DA
q: A boxplot shows Q1 = 25, Q3 = 55. What is the interquartile range?
solution: Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1 = 55 − 25 = 30.
trick: Just subtract: 55 − 25 = 30.

subject: DA
q: In a pie chart where 30% study math, compute the number of non-math students in a class of 2,000.

subject: DA
q: If correlation is -0.3 and standard deviations are 5 and 10, what is the covariance?
solution: Covariance = correlation × SD of X × SD of Y = −0.3 × 5 × 10 = −0.3 × 50 = −15.
trick: 5 × 10 = 50, and 0.3 of 50 is 15. The correlation is negative, so the answer is −15.

subject: DA
q: The number of binary strings of length 5 is
solution: Each of the 5 positions can be 0 or 1, so the number of strings is 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁵ = 32.
trick: Double five times: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. The option 25 is 5², which has the numbers the wrong way round.

subject: DA
q: A normal distribution has a mean of 90 and an SD of 20. What is the z-score for 110?
trick: 110 is 20 above the mean, and one SD is 20, so z = 1.

subject: DA
q: If Bowley's skewness = 0.2, Q1 = 40, Q3 = 80, what is the median?
solution: Bowley's skewness = (Q3 + Q1 − 2 × median) ÷ (Q3 − Q1). So 0.2 = (80 + 40 − 2M) ÷ (80 − 40) = (120 − 2M) ÷ 40, which gives 120 − 2M = 8. So 2M = 112 and the median M = 56.
trick: The midpoint of Q1 and Q3 is 60. Positive skew pulls the median below it by skew × IQR ÷ 2 = 0.2 × 40 ÷ 2 = 4, so the median is 60 − 4 = 56.

subject: DA
q: A stem-and-leaf plot has stem "2" with leaves 1, 3, 5. Which numbers does this represent?
solution: In a stem and leaf plot, the stem holds the leading digit (the tens) and each leaf holds the last digit (the units). With no key shown, stem 2 with leaves 1, 3 and 5 stands for 21, 23 and 25.
trick: Put the stem in front of each leaf: 2 with 1, 3, 5 gives 21, 23, 25.

subject: DA
q: Calculate how many SDs above the mean a 74-inch student is if the mean = 68 inches, standard deviation is 3 inches.
solution: z = (x − mean) ÷ SD = (74 − 68) ÷ 3 = 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so the student is 2 SDs above the mean.

subject: DA
q: A circle graph shows renewables = 25% of 1,000 MW. How many megawatts are NOT from renewables?
solution: Renewables are 25% of 1,000 MW, so the rest is 100% − 25% = 75%. 75% of 1,000 MW = 750 MW.
trick: A quarter of 1,000 is 250, so the other three quarters are 750 MW.

subject: DA
q: If every value in a dataset is multiplied by 3, the standard deviation will ____
solution: The variance would be multiplied by 9, but the standard deviation is measured in the same units as the data. So multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the SD by 3.
trick: SD scales like the data, so it is ×3. The ×9 option is the variance, not the SD.

subject: DA
q: Ten distinct people sit around a round table. How many seatings if two specified people refuse to sit next to each other?
solution: Fix one person to remove rotations, so all seatings = (10 − 1)! = 9! = 362,880. If the two sit together, treat them as one block: (9 − 1)! × 2 = 8! × 2 = 80,640. Not together = 362,880 − 80,640 = 282,240.
trick: Once one of the pair is seated, the other has 9 seats to choose from and 2 are next to them, so 7 out of 9 seatings work. That is 7 × 8! = 7 × 40,320 = 282,240.

subject: DA
q: A bag has 3 red and 9 blue marbles. If 3 marbles are drawn without replacement, what is P(red then blue)?
showNote: Red first is 3/12 and blue next is 9/11, so red then blue is 3/12 × 9/11 = 9/44. The show's 9/11 is only the chance of blue second once a red has come out; 9/44 wasn't among the options.
solution: Red on the first draw and blue on the second is what counts, and the third draw does not matter. Red first is 3/12 = 1/4, and then 9 of the 11 marbles left are blue, so blue next is 9/11. The option 9/11 is just that second step, and none of the three options matches the full answer. Multiply the steps: 1/4 × 9/11 = 9/44.
trick: Multiply the two chances: 3/12 is 1/4, and 1/4 × 9/11 = 9/44. Do not stop at 9/11, which skips the first draw.

subject: DA
q: In a race with 8 runners, how many ways can gold, silver, and bronze medals be awarded?
solution: Gold, silver and bronze go to 3 different runners in order, so the number of ways is 8P3 = 8 × 7 × 6 = 336.
trick: 8 choices for gold, 7 for silver, 6 for bronze: 8 × 7 = 56, then 56 × 6 = 336.

subject: DA
q: What is the mean of the ebook downloads: 25, 50, 75 and 90?
trick: Guess 50. The 25 and 75 cancel out around it and the 50 sits on it, so only 90 matters. It is 40 above, and 40 ÷ 4 = 10, so the mean is 50 + 10 = 60.

subject: DA
q: A bar chart shows heights: A = 5, B = 8, C = 6. Which bar corresponds to the median height?
solution: The median is the middle value when the heights are put in order. In order they are 5, 6, 8, so the median is 6, which is bar C.
trick: Ignore the order of the bars. B is the tallest and A the shortest, so C is the one in the middle.

subject: DA
q: If a wife's selection chance is 3/7 and her husband's is 2/3, what is the probability that neither is selected?
solution: Assuming the two selections are independent, P(neither) = P(wife not selected) × P(husband not selected) = (1 − 3/7) × (1 − 2/3) = 4/7 × 1/3 = 4/21.
trick: Flip each chance: the wife misses with 4/7 and the husband with 1/3. Multiply across: 4 × 1 = 4 over 7 × 3 = 21.

subject: DA
q: Find the sum of all four-digit numbers that can be formed by the digits 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 without repetition.
solution: Each digit appears in each place in 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 of the numbers. The digits add up to 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25, so each place adds up to 24 × 25 = 600. The total is 600 × 1000 + 600 × 100 + 600 × 10 + 600 = 600 × 1111 = 666,600.

subject: DA
q: When two coins are tossed, let E = no tail appears and F = no head appears. Find P(E | F).
solution: Two coins give HH, HT, TH, TT. E (no tail) is only HH and F (no head) is only TT, so they can never happen together. Then P(E | F) = P(E ∩ F) ÷ P(F) = 0 ÷ (1/4) = 0.
